---
title: "CRYSTAL geometry and EOS keywords"
---

This page is a quick reference for the geometry-optimization keywords used in
Laboratory 3. For the scientific explanation, read the Laboratory 3 page.

## Full geometry optimization

```text
OPTGEOM
FULLOPTG
TOLDEG
0.0004
TOLDEX
0.0001
TOLDEE
8
PRINTFORCES
END
```

`FULLOPTG` allows optimization of both cell and symmetry-allowed internal
coordinates.

`TOLDEG` controls the RMS gradient criterion.

`TOLDEX` controls the RMS displacement criterion.

`TOLDEE 8` corresponds to an optimization energy-change threshold of
$10^{-8}$ hartree.

`PRINTFORCES` requests additional atomic-gradient information.

## Constant-volume optimization

For an EOS point:

```text
OPTGEOM
CVOLOPT
TOLDEG
0.0004
TOLDEX
0.0001
TOLDEE
8
END
```

`CVOLOPT` keeps the volume fixed while relaxing any other structural degrees of
freedom allowed by symmetry.

## Why the two calculations are different

A free geometry optimization asks:

> What volume and structure minimize the energy?

A constant-volume optimization asks:

> At this *specified* volume, what structure has the lowest energy?

The second question is the one required for an energy–volume EOS dataset.
